comparator.sourceNotes: The adopted Dutch 2026–2027 regulations set 60 EC in each year. The third year includes 30 EC of approved open study, a 6 EC science and society course, one 6 EC restricted choice and an 18 EC individual research project. Machine Learning is the first-listed of three equally eligible choices. The alternatives are Computational (Pharmaco)Chemistry and System Modeling Project. The language, lab-safety and career-study requirements carry no additional credits. Article 9.1 permits at most a 12 EC shortfall from the first two years on entry to the project, with all practicals passed. The project description normally expects the other required components to be complete. The assessment covers the work, written report and presentation. Clinical physics certification has separate requirements.

exception.reason: UCR can build feasible pathways in biomedical science and health data, and in physical and chemical methods alongside biomedicine. The first develops physiology, biochemistry, molecular laboratory work, numerical methods and medical image analysis. The second also brings in waves, optical spectroscopy, microscopy, chemical testing and instrument-based materials analysis. Those methods are applied largely to environmental and materials questions. VU builds a sustained sequence of physical and chemical measurement for medical questions, including optics, radiation, ultrasound, physiological signals and quantitative clinical chemistry, before an individual research project. UCR’s available combinations do not provide comparable progression from measurement principles through clinical and physiological applications.

exception.ucrCourseEvidence: Two 180 EC internal schedules passed current workbook feasibility. A term swap retains the biomedical and data selections. A second schedule integrates Sustainability Essentials I and II and R3. Neither is presented as an alternative.

candidateAssessment.label: Biomedical Science and Health Data Science
candidateAssessment.reason: A feasible 24-course sequence covers physiology, disease mechanisms, experimental molecular biology, probability, image processing and prediction. Interpreting and processing medical images contributes to diagnostics, while the sequence lacks depth in how instruments acquire the underlying measurements.

candidateAssessment.label: Medical physics reconstruction through sustainability and computation
candidateAssessment.reason: A second feasible 24-course sequence combines physics and chemistry in Sustainability Essentials I and II with R3 instrumentation and biochemical laboratory work. Optical spectroscopy, Fourier wave analysis, electron microscopy, electrochemical recovery and instrument-based materials analysis provide genuine technical overlap. The applications and later progression remain in sustainability and materials, with no sustained experimental medical-physics or clinical analytical-chemistry sequence.

candidateAssessment.label: Molecular diagnostics and bioinformatics
candidateAssessment.reason: Life Science Laboratory, molecular pathology and cell biology provide meaningful molecular diagnostics and introductory bioinformatics, supported by computing and mathematics. They do not establish a sequence in biological network dynamics, sequence and transcriptomics analysis, or measured physiological signal modeling.

audience.programmeDescription: VU Medical Natural Sciences brings physics, chemistry, mathematics and computing together with physiology to investigate disease and medical technology. Students learn experimental measurement, molecular analysis and modelling before completing an individual research project.
audience.comparisonExplanation: UCR offers biomedical laboratory work, quantitative analysis of medical images, and courses that teach optics and chemical measurement through sustainability applications. VU develops these physical and chemical methods in a sustained sequence of medical experiments and measurement. UCR’s available courses cover parts of that sequence.
